earlier_scan.source_named: Sadowsky, Aninao, Cayunao & Heggarty 2015 descriptive chapter on Huilliche/Tsesungun in Linguistica indigena sudamericana; Lenz 1895-97 Estudios araucanos (huilliche dialect texts); neither text reachable with a stress statement online.

new_statements.quote: [p.109] Otras aves de corral, tales como el 'ganso' y el 'pavo', reciben nombres tomados del castellano con las consiguientes adaptaciones fónicas; son bastante comunes las formas gansu y pafu y en la isla Huapi, donde predomina la acentuación oxítona, se encuentran las variantes gansú y pafú. [...] [n.3, p.113] Por otra parte, se recurre a la tilde únicamente para destacar las variantes agudas características de los hablantes de la isla Huapi; en lo demás, se sigue la norma del alfabeto unificado.
new_statements.translation: [p.109] Other farm birds, such as the goose and the turkey, receive names taken from Spanish with the corresponding phonic adaptations; the forms gansu and pafu are quite common, and on Isla Huapi, where oxytone (final) accentuation predominates, one finds the variants gansú and pafú. [...] [n.3] Moreover, the written accent is used only to highlight the oxytone variants characteristic of the Isla Huapi speakers; otherwise the norm of the Alfabeto Unificado is followed.
new_statements.citation: Contreras, Constantino. 1990. Palabras claves del mundo huilliche: observaciones sobre léxico y etnografía. Alpha (Osorno) 6: 103-118.
new_statements.locator: p. 109 (section 9, aves de corral) and note 3, p. 113
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked (all under, present and consistent): 16 pp = Alpha 6: 103-118, image-only, ilovepdf producer) +.; /.pdf. Quote check (Contreras 1990): I rendered PDF page 7 (printed '- 109 -') and page 11 (printed '113') and read them directly. p.109: 'Otras aves de corral, tales como el 'ganso' y el 'pavo', reciben nombres tomados del castellano con las consiguientes adaptaciones fonicas; son bastante comunes las formas gansu y pafu y en la isla Huapi, donde predomina la acentuacion oxitona, se encuentran las variantes gansu' y pafu'.' -- verbatim as reported (scanned lines 242-247 identical). p.113 n.3: 'Empleamos aqui las grafias del alfabeto unificado mapuche con las leves adaptaciones pa…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Only a partial, sub-variety statement exists: among Isla Huapi (Lago Ranco) Huilliche speakers final-syllable (oxytone) accentuation predominates and is flagged as a local peculiarity; for the rest (San Juan de la Costa tsesungun) accent is left unmarked as following the general Mapuche norm, i.e. implicitly the pan-Mapudungun pattern (penult in vowel-final words, final in consonant-final words, per Lenz p.388 n.1 / Salas), which no source states for Huilliche in so many words. Lenz (p. XXIV, with Huilliche examples s'úka ~ s'uká-mo) adds that the accent is weak and positionally unstable, shifting with phrase rhythm.
new_statements.exceptions: Contreras marks non-final accents on some cited forms despite n.3 (súngoll 'olla', pútriwe 'colgador de ollas', kúsuf 'viento') alongside final ones (fotúm, mawún, kuú, ketrú, gansú, pafú); Lenz notes disyllables vary by position in the phrase (s'úka vs s'uká-mo).
new_statements.domain_note: Contreras: lexical citation forms from elicitation interviews (San Juan de la Costa, Isla Huapi, Rupumeica etc.), statement restricted to Isla Huapi speakers. Lenz: word accent described as weak and dependent on 'el ritmo del conjunto' (phrase rhythm) - arguably phrase-level conditioning.
new_statements.identity_note: Contreras 1990's positional statement concerns the Isla Huapi (Lago Ranco, Provincia de Ranco) sub-variety of Huilliche, which he contrasts with the San Juan de la Costa (Osorno coast) variety = tsesungun/chesungun, the core huil1244 variety; both fall under huil1244 (no separate glottocodes). Lenz 1895-97's accent remarks are framed for 'araucano' in general but sit inside the introduction to his Huilliche text (Estudio I, speaker Domingo Quintuprai of Osorno) and use Huilliche example forms (s'uka = ruka). The Alvarez-Santullano et al. 2016 RLA study covers Lanco, Panguipulli, Maihue, Rupumeica and Aleucapi (Los Rios/Los Lagos 'territorio huilliche'), partly transitional to central Mapudungun (mapu1245).

sources.note: p.109: in Isla Huapi 'predomina la acentuación oxítona' (gansú, pafú vs. gansu, pafu elsewhere); n.3 p.113: tilde used only to mark the 'variantes agudas características de los hablantes de la isla Huapi', otherwise the Alfabeto Unificado norm is followed. Only Huilliche-specific positional remark found; partial (one sub-variety).

sources.citation: Molineaux, Benjamin. 2014. Synchronic and diachronic morphoprosody: stress and affix status in Mapudungun. DPhil, Oxford. (sec. 5.4.2.1, pp. 273-276)
sources.note: Second-hand: notes Lenz's Huilliche texts are the most richly stress-marked; marked stresses rarely fall off the rightmost pattern (kuʎín, wüʈ͡ʂé-n, muŋé-j-m-i), disyllabic V-final words vary (mápu-mo); treats them with caution as not ancestral to the central variety he analyses.

sources.citation: Lenz, Rodolfo. 1895-1897. Estudios araucanos. Santiago: Imprenta Cervantes. (Introducción 'De la lengua araucana' p. XXIV; Estudio I 'Viaje al país de los manzaneros, dialecto huilliche' p. 6; Estudio X p. 388 n.1)
sources.note: p. XXIV (with Huilliche examples): 'El acento tiene poca fuerza i poca estabilidad; a menudo cambia su lugar segun leyes poco fijas de equilibrio: Tëfámu mëli ñi s'úka... pero ñi s'uká-mo këpán'. p.6 (intro to Huilliche text): accent in araucano generally not strong, fluctuates over syllables with phrase rhythm; he marks it only when strong or in an unusual position. p.388 n.1 (Pehuenche songs): Valdivia's rule still generally holds - penult stress, final when the word ends in a consonant.
